Fabrication technique
The fabrication process is ﬁrst developed on bulk Si
substrates (Fig. 1) and subsequently adapted to SOI sub-
strates to demonstrate process transferability. The refer-
ence architecture consists of suspended Si NWs anchored
at both ends and released from the substrate while
remaining at the top surface. This geometry enables
integration with surrounding device structures.
Fabrication is carried out on a (100)-oriented Si sub-
strate with a thickness of 525 µm and resistivity of
1–100 Ω cm. The diced chip size is 15 mm × 15 mm. The
process begins with standard solvent cleaning using
acetone, an isopropyl alcohol (IPA) rinse, and N2 blow-
drying. A 100 nm SiO2 layer is then deposited by plasma-
enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) at 90 °C
(Fig. 1a). NW patterns are deﬁned using electron-beam
lithography (EBL) using PMMA resist, achieving a critical

During the measurement, the device was biased at

This study addresses that gap by developing a furnace-
free route for suspended sub-100 nm Si NW fabrication.
Building on the nanoscale protrusion and DRIE-release
strategy of earlier SCREAM-derived Si NW work, the
present process replaces the oxide/LPCVD-type sidewall-
protection step with sacriﬁcial PVD Cr sidewall coating.
The Cr coating preserves the nanoscale Si preform
linewidth during DRIE release, enabling suspended Si
NWs with critical dimensions down to 50 nm, aspect
ratios up to 100, and array pitches of 5 µm, while limiting
the maximum process temperature to 180 °C. The process
is implemented on both bulk Si and SOI substrates; bulk
Si is used to validate morphology and process transfer-
ability, while SOI enables electrically addressable devices,
including two-terminal NWs and a suspended junction-
less FET architecture.
